description: Subject: Urgent: Addressing the Absence and Maintenance of Rain Storm Water Drainage Systems Respected Sir/Madam, I am Kannan Madhavan R from Chennai, Tamil Nadu-[postcode removed], India, and I am Writing to Draw your Urgent Attention to a Critical Issue thats Affecting the Residents of Chennai. We, the People of Chennai, are Hardworking Individuals Striving to Sustain for our Basic Needs such as Food, Clothing, and Shelter. Despite our Harsh Conditions, we Diligently Pay all our Taxes (Property Tax, CMWSSB Tax, GST, TAN, VAT, TDS etc.) to the Government in Advance. This is All Ours Hard-Earned Money, and We Believe It is Our Right to Expect Basic Amenities in Return. Unfortunately, there Seems to be a Lack of Responsiveness and Humanity from the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) in Addressing the Fundamental Infrastructure Needs, Specifically the Construction and Maintenance of Rain Storm Water Drainage Systems. Since 2015, Numerous Online and Offline Complaints have been Raised with the GCC, CMWSSB, Tamil Nadu CM Cell, and other Highest Officials, as well as through CPGRAMS. Despite these Efforts, We have Not seen Substantial Action Taken to Address the Extreme Water Stagnation and Flooding Issues in Zones 1 to Zone-15 of Chennai City. Root Cause of these Issues is the Absence of Rain Storm Water Drainage Canals & its Catch Pits, and Irregular Desilting of Existing Catch Pits and Canals. The Irregular Cleaning of these Drainage Systems Exacerbates the Problem much More. This Negligence has Resulted in Revere Water Stagnation and Flooding during the Monsoon Seasons of 2005, 2008, 2010, 2015, 2017, 2020, and most recently, 2023. Many Homes in our Neighborhoods are at a Lower Ground Level, making them Particularly Vulnerable to Water Stagnation. The Recurrent Flooding has Not only Threatened Our Lives but also Caused Significant Damage to Our Properties and Valuable Belongings. Additionally, the Stagnant water has Led to the Outbreak of Hazardous Infectious Diseases such as Malaria and Chikungunya. Attached are Images that Documents the Water Stagnation we Experience even During Minor Rainfall, which escalates Dramatically during Heavy Rains. Despite these Visual Testimonies, there Remains an Absence of Adequate Rain Storm Water Drainage Systems across All the Wards in All the Parts in All zones of GCC. In contrast, whereas the nearby Cties in Other states have More Effective Rain Storm Water Drainage Systems. On Behalf of All the Residents in the Streets, Areas, and Localities across Chennai, Earnestly i Request your Immediate Intervention. That is We Require the Construction of New Rain Storm Water Drainage Canals and Catch Pits Every 10 Meters, as Stipulated by the New GCC and Tamil Nadu government Rules and Regulations. Additionally, Looking Forward to Properly & Regular Desilt the all Existing Drainage Systems across the City. We Implore You to Take Swift Action to Mitigate these Issues and Improve Our Living Conditions. Thank you in Advance for your Attention and Assistance. Sincerely, Kannan Madhavan R

description: I hope this letter finds you in good health. During the rainy season, the streets often get waterlogged, posing a threat to public health and damaging property. This situation has become a matter of great concern for the residents. Last year myself and my daughter suffered with dengue. The absence of proper drainage not only affects our daily lives but also raises the risk of waterborne diseases in the area. Moreover, it hampers the overall cleanliness and hygiene of our street. Our neighborhood streets drainage system have been modernized. But our ponnappa street remains with same old drainage system. I kindly request your intervention in this matter to initiate the necessary steps for the improvement and modernization of the drainage system in our locality. I believe that your timely action on this issue will significantly enhance the living conditions for the residents of our ponnappa Street. Reputation Damage: If a store sells rotten fruit, it risks damaging its reputation, which can lead to a loss of customer trust and a decline in business. description: Subject: Urgent: Addressing the Absence and Maintenance of Rain Storm Water Drainage Systems Respected Sir/Madam, I am Sethukkarasi R from 14 / 31, K.R. Koil Street, West Mambalam, Chennai, Tamil Nadu-[postcode removed], India which Comes under Division-140, Part-30 and Kodambakkam Zone-10 Greater Chennai Corporation, and I am Writing to Draw your Urgent Attention to a Critical Issue thats Affecting the Residents of Chennai. We, the People of Chennai, are Hardworking Individuals Striving to Sustain for our Basic Needs such as Food, Clothing, and Shelter. Despite our Harsh Conditions, we Diligently Pay all our Taxes (Property Tax, CMWSSB Tax, GST, TAN, VAT, TDS etc.) to the Government in Advance. This is All Ours Hard-Earned Money, and We Believe It is Our Right to Expect Basic Amenities in Return. Unfortunately, there Seems to be a Lack of Responsiveness and Humanity from the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) in Addressing the Fundamental Infrastructure Needs, Specifically the Construction and Maintenance of Rain Storm Water Drainage Systems. Since 2015, Numerous Online and Offline Complaints have been Raised with the GCC, CMWSSB, Tamil Nadu CM Cell, and other Highest Officials, as well as through CPGRAMS. Despite these Efforts, We have Not seen Substantial Action Taken to Address the Extreme Water Stagnation and Flooding Issues in Zones 1 to Zone-15 of Chennai City. Root Cause of these Issues is the Absence of Rain Storm Water Drainage Canals & its Catch Pits, and Irregular Desilting of Existing Catch Pits and Canals. The Irregular Cleaning of these Drainage Systems Exacerbates the Problem much More. description: Subject: Urgent: Addressing the Absence and Maintenance of Rain Storm Water Drainage Systems Respected Sir/Madam, I am Ravi A from 14 / 31, K.R. Koil Street, West Mambalam, Chennai, Tamil Nadu-[postcode removed], India which Comes under Division-140, Part-30 and Kodambakkam Zone-10 Greater Chennai Corporation, and I am Writing to Draw your Urgent Attention to a Critical Issue thats Affecting the Residents of Chennai. We, the People of Chennai, are Hardworking Individuals Striving to Sustain for our Basic Needs such as Food, Clothing, and Shelter. Despite our Harsh Conditions, we Diligently Pay all our Taxes (Property Tax, CMWSSB Tax, GST, TAN, VAT, TDS etc.) to the Government in Advance. This is All Ours Hard-Earned Money, and We Believe It is Our Right to Expect Basic Amenities in Return. Unfortunately, there Seems to be a Lack of Responsiveness and Humanity from the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) in Addressing the Fundamental Infrastructure Needs, Specifically the Construction and Maintenance of Rain Storm Water Drainage Systems. Since 2015, Numerous Online and Offline Complaints have been Raised with the GCC, CMWSSB, Tamil Nadu CM Cell, and other Highest Officials, as well as through CPGRAMS. Despite these Efforts, We have Not seen Substantial Action Taken to Address the Extreme Water Stagnation and Flooding Issues in Zones 1 to Zone-15 of Chennai City. Root Cause of these Issues is the Absence of Rain Storm Water Drainage Canals & its Catch Pits, and Irregular Desilting of Existing Catch Pits and Canals. The Irregular Cleaning of these Drainage Systems Exacerbates the Problem much More. This Negligence has Resulted in Revere Water Stagnation and Flooding during the Monsoon Seasons of 2005, 2008, 2010, 2015, 2017, 2020, and most recently, 2023. Many Homes in our Neighborhoods are at a Lower Ground Level, making them Particularly Vulnerable to Water Stagnation. The Recurrent Flooding has Not only Threatened Our Lives but also Caused Significant Damage to Our Properties and Valuable Belongings. Additionally, the Stagnant water has Led to the Outbreak of Hazardous Infectious Diseases such as Malaria and Chikungunya. Attached are Images that Documents the Water Stagnation we Experience even During Minor Rainfall, which escalates Dramatically during Heavy Rains. Despite these Visual Testimonies, there Remains an Absence of Adequate Rain Storm Water Drainage Systems across All the Wards in All the Parts in All zones of GCC. In contrast, whereas the nearby Cities in Other states have More Effective Rain Storm Water Drainage Systems. On Behalf of All the Residents in the Streets, Areas, and Localities across Chennai, Earnestly i Request your Immediate Intervention. That is We Require the Construction of New Rain Storm Water Drainage Canals and Catch Pits Every 10 Meters, as Stipulated by the New GCC and Tamil Nadu government Rules and Regulations. Additionally, Looking Forward to Properly & Regular Desilt the all Existing Drainage Systems across the City. We Implore you to Take Swift Action to Mitigate these Issues and Improve Our Living Conditions. Thank you in Advance for your Attention and Assistance. Sincerely, Ravi A

description: I am writing to express my growing concern and frustration regarding the persistent issue of street cats defecating in and around our apartment complex. This problem has escalated to an intolerable level, significantly affecting the quality of life for all residents. For several months now, we have been dealing with an increasing number of stray cats that roam freely around our apartment premises. While some residents might find their presence benign, the reality is quite the opposite. These cats frequently defecate in public areas, including walkways, and even near the entrances of our apartments. This not only creates an unsightly mess but also poses serious health risks, especially for young children who play in these areas. The smell of cat feces is pervasive, and despite our efforts to clean up, the problem persists. The constant need to remove cat waste from common areas has become a daily chore for many of us, adding unnecessary stress and inconvenience to our lives. Furthermore, this issue has attracted other pests, exacerbating the situation. I understand that stray cats are part of the urban environment, but when their activities start to impact the cleanliness and hygiene of our living space, it becomes a matter that needs immediate attention. We have tried various deterrents and community-driven cleanup efforts, but these measures have proven to be ineffective in the long term. I am requesting the intervention of the appropriate authorities or animal control services to address this issue comprehensively. Specifically, I urge the implementation of a program to humanely capture and relocate these street cats away from our apartment complex. Additionally, measures to prevent other strays from entering the premises should be considered, such as secure fencing or deterrent devices. It is essential for the well-being of all residents that this matter is addressed promptly. We deserve to live in a clean, safe, and healthy environment without the constant worry of encountering cat feces. I trust that you will understand the gravity of this situation and take the necessary steps to resolve it effectively. Thank you for your attention to this pressing issue. We look forward to a prompt and positive response. Sincerely, Vinod Kumar A M

description: This letter serves to clarify the circumstances regarding the property tax demand associated with the land and buildings located at No. 1, Brindavan Nagar and No. 63/15, Thiruvalluvar Street. Background of Property Acquisition and Development: The land was acquired approximately 40 years ago, with a residential building constructed thereafter. A non-residential building was recently constructed on the same land, but at a different location on the property. Current Land Records and Taxation Issues: The existing land records pertain solely to the land itself and do not account for the superstructures (buildings) erected subsequently. As a result, the property tax demand has, to date, been linked exclusively to the address No. 1, Brindavan Nagar, referring to the residential building. It is pertinent to note that the non-residential building was constructed at the rear side of the property, separate from the residential building, and corresponds to the address No. 63/15, Thiruvalluvar Street. Request for Rectification in Property Tax Records: To ensure clarity and avoid any future discrepancies, we request the property tax demand for the non-residential building to reflect its actual location as No. 63/15, Thiruvalluvar Street. This differentiation is essential as both buildings, although located on the same plot of land, serve distinct purposes and are associated with separate addresses for functional and administrative convenience. Electricity and Utility Records: The electricity connection and related records for the non-residential building are also registered under No. 63/15, Thiruvalluvar Street. Therefore, aligning the property tax demand with this address will ensure consistency across all utility and tax records. Conclusion: We kindly request that a separate property tax demand be issued for the non-residential building under the address No. 63/15, Thiruvalluvar Street. This amendment will facilitate the payment of property tax and prevent any potential conflicts arising from misaligned addresses in the future. Additionally, the presence of a cell tower would likely reduce property values in our neighborhood, making it less appealing to prospective buyers who may share these health concerns. The visual impact and intrusion on our skyline also disrupt the aesthetic harmony of our community. We kindly urge your corporation to consider alternative locations, such as commercial or industrial areas, where the tower could be placed without negatively impacting residential areas. We believe a solution that balances your need for improved coverage with our community’s quality of life is possible. Thank you for your attention to this matter. description: I am writing to bring to your attention a significant issue that the residents of JK Avenue in PTC Quarters, Thoraipakkam have been facing for quite some time. The problem concerns the rampant and indiscriminate parking of vehicles on our street, which has severely impacted the daily lives of the residents. Over the past few months, the situation has worsened, with numerous vehicles being parked along the sides of the street, often occupying both sides. This has left little to no room for the movement of other vehicles, making it extremely challenging for residents to commute. The street has effectively turned into a makeshift parking lot, causing significant inconvenience. The most pressing issue is that these vehicles often belong to individuals who do not reside on our street. Many outsiders use our street for parking due to its proximity to nearby commercial areas and shops. This not only congests the street but also makes it impossible for residents to find adequate parking spaces for their vehicles. In some cases, the situation has escalated to the point where residents cannot bring their cars into the street, which is especially problematic during emergencies or for elderly and disabled residents who require easy access. The narrow width of the street exacerbates the problem, as there are no gaps left between the parked vehicles, further restricting movement. This creates a potential safety hazard, as emergency vehicles like ambulances would find it difficult, if not impossible, to navigate through the street in case of an emergency. We, the residents of JK Avenue, kindly request the Chennai Corporation Office to take immediate action to address this issue. We suggest the implementation of stricter parking regulations, including the designation of specific parking areas and the installation of no-parking signs in critical zones. Additionally, regular monitoring and enforcement of these rules by traffic authorities would help in mitigating the problem. We believe that your prompt intervention will significantly improve the quality of life on our street. We appreciate your attention to this matter and look forward to a positive and swift resolution

description: Dear Sir/Madam, I am writing to bring to your attention the challenges we are facing in correcting the parents’ names in my daughter’s birth certificate, which was issued by the Chennai Corporation ( Division 198, Zone 15). Due to this discrepancy, we are experiencing significant mental and physical distress while trying to apply for her Aadhaar card. On February 1st, 2025, we visited the Chennai Corporation office(Division 198, Zone 15) and submitted a written request along with Aadhaar proof to update the parents’ names as per Aadhaar records. However, on February 13th, 2025, I received a call from the Corporation office instructing us to obtain a letter from the hospital where my daughter was born. Following this, my spouse, along with our 2-year-old child, visited Apollo Cradle Hospital to obtain the required letter. The hospital, however, insisted that we first provide an affidavit. Despite spending ₹1,000 to obtain the affidavit, the hospital is now asking for multiple corrections, leading to unnecessary delays and complications. Both the Corporation and the hospital are making this process extremely difficult, and as working professionals, it is not feasible for us to take frequent leaves to follow up on these matters repeatedly. We seek your immediate intervention to ensure a streamlined and fair resolution. If necessary, I am prepared to escalate this issue further, including addressing it to the Honorable Chief Minister. I request your urgent assistance in resolving this matter at the earliest. Looking forward to your prompt response. Best regards, Ramu

description: Sir/Madam We are residents of K block 16th street, Anna Nagar East and wish to bring to your attention the following issues which are of great concern. 1. Our street has been re-laid with poor road levelling leading to flooding in the middle of the street which is knee deep and does not permit any vehicle movement during monsoons. There are several senior citizens and bed ridden inmates and any vehicle transport or ambulances also cannot access the houses. The storm water drain system which is laid only on one side of the street is more than 50 years old and is partly blocked and grossly inadequate to drain the storm/rain water of even mild rains. 2. The recently constructed Bougainvilla park has been built at higher level and we note with serious concern that it does not have a rain water drainage system leading to frequent flooding and stagnation of water inside the park. The park officials resort to temporary pumping out of the stagnant, stinking and unhygienic flood waters of the park into 16th street leading to further misery, mosquito breeding and related health issues/agony for the residents. 3. Repeated flooding of the houses in 16th street has led to damage of parked vehicles, household furniture and home appliances such as fridges, washing machines etc which have needed replacement at enormous costs. We’re writing this letter as a joint petition to take immediate action to relieve us of the suffering during the monsoons. Please find attached photo documentation/videos of the issues highlighted above
